original_metadata.title: Boundary persistence and charged-set repulsion for vertexical differential-inclusion families on all finite hypercubes under opposite-face persistence and charged-vertex repulsion
original_metadata.author: Manoj Gopalkrishnan; Ezra Miller; Anne Shiu
original_metadata.source_title: A Projection Argument for Differential Inclusions, with Applications to Persistence of Mass-Action Kinetics
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof combines induction on face dimension with a projection argument in shrinking face blocks, retaining a fixed lower-dimensional inclusion while trajectory time is reparametrized. Its key obligation is to transfer uniform vertex-repulsion neighborhoods back to face repulsion, rather than merely showing that an individual trajectory cannot converge to a corner.

proof_review.note: Read full Theorem3.15 and exact trajectory/persistence/repulsion definitions2.3-2.5, Remarks2.11-2.13, face-block and vertexical definitions3.1-3.14. Index family is all finite nonempty subsets of positive integers; repulsing setR can be infinite. Each member is persistent relative to all opposite faces and repelled by charged vertices. Both conclusions retained: entire-boundary persistence and charged-set repulsion, with whole-boundary repulsion only under the extra opposite-face repulsion assumption. The new proof supplies both face claims and the uniform fixed-Y projection estimate, allowing order-preserving continuous time changes. No mass-action application, permanence consequence, or strongly-endotactic theorem6.11 whose proof is deferred is counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem3.15 parts1-2 as one main unit for exactly Definition3.13 vertexical families and Definition3.14 charged/opposite faces. Persistence uses closure disjointness and repulsion uses uniform nested neighborhoods Definition2.4. This is conditional abstract differential-inclusion structure, not an unconditional weakly-reversible/global-attractor theorem.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: Full original Theorem 3.15 and its complete two-face-claim structural-induction proof are retained with all trajectory, persistence, uniform repulsion, face/block, projection, charged-set and vertexical-family definitions. The index family contains all finite nonempty subsets of positive integers; the repulsing index set may be infinite. Both charged-set repulsion and whole-boundary persistence conclusions remain, with whole-boundary repulsion only under the additional opposite-face repulsion hypothesis. The fixed lower-dimensional differential inclusion and uniform distance estimate, independent of the particular trajectory/subinterval, are supplied; order-preserving continuous time changes remain allowed. Original geometric figures are assets and all proof language/math stays editable. No mass-action application, permanence consequence or deferred strongly-endotactic theorem is selected.
